title: Joint Relocation
statementMd:
VegiCat owns a company with n𝑛 employees in k𝑘 nonempty teams. The employees live along a straight road, represented by a number line. VegiCat wants to arrange two meeting points for them.

VegiCat divides the teams into two sets, A𝐴 and B𝐵, with each team in exactly one set. He chooses a meeting point for each set at any real coordinate. **All employees on the same team must go to the same meeting point.** Each team in set A𝐴 goes to the meeting point for A𝐴, and each team in set B𝐵 goes to the meeting point for B𝐵. Either set may be empty.

Let SA𝑆𝐴 list the home positions of all employees on teams in A𝐴, and define SB𝑆𝐵 similarly for B𝐵. Each employee is counted separately, even when home positions repeat.

For a list S=(x1,x2,…,xm)𝑆=(𝑥1,𝑥2,…,𝑥𝑚) of home positions, the minimum total distance for these employees to travel to one meeting point is M(S)=minp∈Rm∑j=1|xj−p|.

Define M(S)=0 when S is empty. Help VegiCat minimize M(SA)+M(SB) over all ways to divide the teams into the two sets.

## Input

The first line contains an integer T (1≤T≤3⋅105), the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two integers n and k (1≤k≤n≤3⋅105), denoting the number of employees and the number of teams, respectively.

Each of the next k lines describes one team. The i-th line contains an integer mi (1≤mi≤n), the number of employees on team i, followed by mi integers xi,1,…,xi,mi (1≤xi,j≤107), their home positions. The sum of all mi in a test case is n.

Home positions may repeat and may be given in any order.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 3⋅105.

## Output

For each test case, output an integer — the minimum possible total travel distance.

## Note

In the first test case, VegiCat sends team 1 to a meeting point at position 1 and team 2 to a meeting point at position 8. The employees in each team travel a total distance of 2, giving the answer 4.

In the second test case, VegiCat chooses meeting points at 3 and 9. He sends teams 1 and 2 to the first meeting point, and team 3 to the second. The employees in teams 1, 2, and 3 travel total distances of 12, 1, and 2, respectively, giving the answer 15.
